title: Frostline Zero
observed_goal: The page text describes the goal as outrunning the avalanche and reaching the finish line; only the main menu and background scene are visible in the screenshots, and the goal was not observed during active game execution.
observed_controls: Page text: AD / left and right keys for steering
Page text: Space / W / up key for jumping, with the option to hold for greater height
Page text: Shift for air slam and boosting on large drops
Page text: S / down key for braking
Page text: R to restart and Esc to pause
Page text: WASD and arrow keys for two-player mode; the exact player assignments are stated on the page
observed_core_loop: not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive; no frame, repeated cycle, run start, collision, complete jump, or return to a reproducible state was recorded.
progress_feedback: The page shows the phrases Personal best, Stage 1, No finish yet, 0 clears, and 0 deaths; in-game progress, distance to the finish, or outcome feedback was not observed.
decisions_risk_reward: The page text mentions the risk of collision and destruction after one hit and lists steering, jumping, braking, and air slam controls; choice and trade-offs during active game execution were not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
rewards: The page text refers to finish, personal best, and clears; actual rewards, scoring, or content unlocking were not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
penalties_failure: The page text claims that one hit causes the run to end, and the official card mentions outrunning the avalanche; failure or an outcome screen was not observed in the frames.
outcomes_replay: The page text contains the Restart run option, but its execution, winning, losing, run completion, or replay cycle was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
onboarding: The main menu displays textual control instructions and the Start Run option; entry into active gameplay and interactive instruction were not observed.
visual_audio_accessibility: The screenshots show a readable, high-contrast menu, textual control labels, and a 3D/snowy background. Audio was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive; only a technical AudioContext error was recorded. Accessibility settings were not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
technical_clues: A canvas with dimensions 1280×800 is recorded in the metadata; this is only a technical clue and does not establish game behavior.

The metadata records 8 scripts, one stylesheet, three fonts, one image, and several fetch/ping requests; script bytes and engine markers were not scanned, so no conclusion is drawn about the implementation.
A console warning says that AudioContext was not permitted to start after a user gesture; this is a technical clue about audio status, not proof of the presence or absence of game audio.
A WebGL software fallback warning and one 403 error were recorded; their effect on the game experience is not clear from the inputs.
Changes between frames may be caused by animation or elapsed time; the metadata explicitly says that input acceptance was not proven.
transferable_principles: Present goals, controls, and feedback clearly and visibly before entering the core loop.
Risk should be accompanied by immediate, recognizable feedback, but do not infer balance from menu-only frames.
For testability, design a short, repeatable loop with a start, decision, consequence, and opportunity to repeat.
Keep official claims separate from genuinely observed behavior, and do not treat temporal image changes alone as evidence of input acceptance.
candle_climber_relevance: For Candle Climber, treat only the general principle of clearly displaying controls, danger, and feedback as transferable; do not reproduce any asset, name, text, or appearance from this game.
Tie score/rank only to player skill and performance, not to purchases or wallet and not to a paid advantage.
Do not introduce a free brake, horizontal direction change, or branching route requiring new controls; if such an option is examined, treat it solely as a hypothesis requiring separate testing.
Do not draw a definitive conclusion about the loop, outcome, or feeling of control from this sample, because active execution and outcome were not observed in the frames.
do_not_copy: Do not copy or propose the name, character, visual style, environment, text, audio, brand, or assets of Frostline Zero.
Do not reproduce the official card's claim about the route, obstacles, or run length as a confirmed capability.
Do not present a change in menu selection state or differences between frames as accepted input or game progress.
Do not use a branching route requiring new controls, a free brake, or any purchase/wallet-dependent advantage in Candle Climber.

evidence.claim: The main menu remains in all submitted frames, and active execution or a run start is not visible; the Start Run option and controls panel are visible in the frames.
The after_start frame also shows the main menu; the brightening/visual change of the selected option alone does not prove acceptance of Start or game execution.
The after_key_burst frame still shows the main menu, the No finish yet status, and 0 clears · 0 deaths; key execution or active gameplay was not confirmed.
The after_combined_input frame shows the background scene and main menu, with no direct finish or death visible.
The late frame also shows the main menu, and the No finish yet, 0 clears, and 0 deaths statuses have not changed.
The controls page displays steering, jumping, air slam, braking, restarting, and pausing with the corresponding keys.
The page text states that the goal is to reach the finish under avalanche pressure, with the risk of ending after one hit.

The official game card claims that a 2.3-kilometer hand-crafted route, gaps, glowing rails, and an avalanche pursuit exist; this claim was not playtested through complete game execution in this evidence.
The metadata records that visual interaction may be caused by animation or elapsed time and that input acceptance was not proven.
The metadata records a canvas with dimensions 1280×800 and AudioContext warnings, a WebGL software fallback, and a 403 error; these are only technical clues.

limitations: Only the metadata-and-capture-evidence file and five frames of this game were reviewed; no web browsing, rerun of the game, or hidden control was performed. start_action is none, capture has partial status, some screenshots timed out, and the recorded input is not a game-specific playtest. Therefore, the game loop, outcome, audio, accessibility, scoring, obstacles, and actual control behavior were not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive. The absence of an element in the initial frame does not prove its absence from the entire game.
